arxiv-2111-06726.creator: Dongda Li, Zhaoquan Gu, Yuexuan Wang, Changwei Ren, Francis C.M. Lau
arxiv-2111-06726.description: Abstract Recent studies have revealed that neural combinatorial optimization (NCO) has advantages over conventional algorithms in many combinatorial optimization problems such as routing, but it is less efficient for more complicated optimization tasks such as packing which involves mutually conditioned action spaces.

arxiv-2301-10830.title: Counting Parking Sequences and Parking Assortments Through Permutations Thanks: P. E. Harris was supported through a Karen Uhlenbeck EDGE Fellowship.
arxiv-2301-10830.creator: Spencer J. Franks, Pamela E. Harris, Kimberly Harry, Jan Kretschmann, Megan Vance
arxiv-2301-10830.description: Abstract . Parking sequences (a generalization of parking functions) are defined by specifying car lengths and requiring that a car attempts to park in the first available spot after its preference. If it does not fit there, then a collision occurs and the car fails to park.

arxiv-2307-13367.title: The minimum measurable eccentricity from gravitational waves of LISA massive black hole binaries 2023 The minimum measurable eccentricity from gravitational waves of LISA massive black hole binaries – 15
arxiv-2307-13367.creator: Mudit Garg, Shubhanshu Tiwari, Andrea Derdzinski, John G. Baker, Sylvain Marsat, and Lucio Mayer
arxiv-2307-13367.description: Abstract We explore the eccentricity measurement threshold of LISA for gravitational waves radiated by massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) with redshifted BH masses M z M_{z} in the range 10 4.5 10^{4.5} – 10 7.5 ​ M ☉ 10^{7.5}~{\rm M}_{☉} at redshift z = 1 z=1 .

arxiv-2311-05286.title: Causal Inference from Text: Unveiling Interactions between Variables
arxiv-2311-05286.creator: Yuxiang Zhou, Yulan He
arxiv-2311-05286.description: Abstract Adjusting for latent covariates is crucial for estimating causal effects from observational textual data. Most existing methods only account for confounding covariates that affect both treatment and outcome , potentially leading to biased causal effects. This bias arises from insufficient consideration of non-confounding covariates, which are relevant only to either the treatment or the outcome.

arxiv-2403-00698.title: Path Tracking using Echoes in an Unknown Environment: the Issue of Symmetries and How to Break Them
arxiv-2403-00698.creator: Mireille Boutin, Gregor Kemper
arxiv-2403-00698.description: Abstract . This paper deals with the problem of reconstructing the path of a vehicle in an unknown environment consisting of planar structures using sound. Many systems in the literature do this by using a loudspeaker and microphones mounted on a vehicle. Symmetries in the environment lead to solution ambiguities for such systems.

arxiv-2405-05871.title: The Iwasawa μ \mu -invariant of certain elliptic curves of analytic rank zero
arxiv-2405-05871.creator: Adithya Chakravarthy
arxiv-2405-05871.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Adithya Chakravarthy. This paper is about the Iwasawa theory of elliptic curves over the cyclotomic 𝐙 p \mathbf{Z}_{p} -extension 𝐐 cyc \mathbf{Q}_{\text{cyc}} of 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} . We discuss a deep conjecture of Greenberg that if E / 𝐐 E/\mathbf{Q} is an elliptic curve with good ordinary reduction at p p , and E ⁡ [ p ] E[p] is irreducible as a Galois module, then the Selmer group of E E over 𝐐 cyc \mathbf{Q}_{\text{cyc}} has μ \mu -invariant zero.

arxiv-2503-10957.title: Predicting Stock Movement with BERTweet and Transformers
arxiv-2503-10957.creator: Michael Charles Albada, Mojolaoluwa Joshua Sonola
arxiv-2503-10957.description: Abstract Applying deep learning and computational intelligence to finance has been a popular area of applied research, both within academia and industry, and continues to attract active attention. The inherently high volatility and non-stationary of the data pose substantial challenges to machine learning models, especially so for today’s expressive and highly-parameterized deep learning models.

arxiv-2508-07613.title: UMRE: A Unified Monotonic Transformation for Ranking Ensemble in Recommender Systems
arxiv-2508-07613.creator: Zhengrui Xu Beijing Jiaotong University Beijing, China zrxu23@bjtu.edu.cn Zhe Yang Kuaishou Technology Beijing, China yangzhe03@kuaishou.com Zhengxiao Guo Kuaishou Technology Beijing, China guozhengxiao@kuaishou.com Shukai Liu Kuaishou Technology Beijing, China shukailiu89@gmail.com Luocheng Lin Kua
arxiv-2508-07613.description: Abstract Industrial recommender systems commonly rely on ensemble sorting (ES) to combine predictions from multiple behavioral objectives. Traditionally, this process depends on manually designed nonlinear transformations (e.g., polynomial or exponential functions) and hand-tuned fusion weights to balance competing goals—an approach that is labor-intensive and frequently suboptimal in achieving Pareto efficiency.

pmc-11391615.title: A rare case of superior mesenteric venous and portal vein thrombosis in complicated appendicitis
pmc-11391615.creator: John Paul Bustamante, Claire Caplan, Joanna Sajdlowska, Zamaan Hooda, Melissa Warta
pmc-11391615.description: Superior mesenteric venous (SMV) thrombosis is a rare complication of severe appendicitis. Early recognition is due to improved imaging modalities, which ultimately lead to more prompt intervention. Despite being an uncommon phenomenon, SMV thrombosis can have complications stemming from venous hypertension, such as gastric and esophageal varices, bowel ischemia, sepsis, and death.

pmc-11645895.title: Analysis of Acupoint Selection and Combinations in Acupuncture Treatment of Migraine: A Protocol for Data Mining
pmc-11645895.creator: Yujun He, Yachao Wu, Xiaojun Li
pmc-11645895.description: BackgroundMigraine is a prevalent neurological condition that causes significant disability and has a profound impact on sufferers’ ability to work and their overall quality of life. The efficacy of acupuncture in the treatment of migraines has been confirmed via extensive clinical research.

pmc-12429841.title: Monothiooxalamide–Benzothiazole Hybrids: Predictive Docking on HDAC6, Synthesis, Molecular Structure, and Antiproliferative Activity on Breast Cancer Cells
pmc-12429841.creator: Carlos Eduardo Macías-Hernández, Irving Balbuena-Rebolledo, Efrén V. García-Báez, Laura C. Cabrera-Pérez, Marycarmen Godínez-Victoria, Martha C. Rosales-Hernández, Itzia I. Padilla-Martínez
pmc-12429841.description: A new family of monothiooxalamide derived from 2-aminobenzothiazole was synthesized with the purpose of investigating its anticancer activity. The design of the compounds was focused on targeting the HDAC6 enzyme, a target for antineoplastic drugs. The in silico affinity of compounds to HDAC6 was performed and confirmed by docking simulation.

pmc-13196089.title: Bacterial profile, antimicrobial resistance patterns and associated factors among cancer patients at Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Sidama region, Southern Ethiopia
pmc-13196089.creator: Alemitu Beyene, Demissie Assegu Fenta, Yared Merid
pmc-13196089.description: BackgroundInfectious diseases are the leading cause of morbidity and mortality among cancer patients due to impaired immunity and the immunosuppressive effect of cancer treatment. Therefore, the aim of this study was to determine the bacterial profile, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and factors associated among cancer patients at Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Sidama region, Southern Ethiopia.

pmc-13232280.title: Receptive-field sizes during remapping and uniform transsaccadic updating across the visual space
pmc-13232280.creator: Yiming Wang, Mingsha Zhang, Ning Qian
pmc-13232280.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryForward receptive-field (RF) remapping, a mechanism for transsaccadic updating of retinal positions and perceptual stability, transiently changes cells’ eccentricities and thus could also change their RF sizes, yet few studies examined RF sizes during remapping. A related issue is how the mechanism ensures the desired uniform updating across the visual space – a subtraction of the saccade vector from stimuli’s retinal positions wherever they appear – given highly nonuniform RF sizes and cortical magnification over eccentricities.
